form_analysis.feedback: Comprehensive aftercare form for general laser scar reduction (fractional, non-ablative). Provides excellent phased guidance through healing and collagen remodeling. Strong emphasis on scar-specific care including massage timing, silicone use, and realistic improvement expectations. Good coverage of different scar types and response variations.

form_data.introduction: This aftercare protocol is for fractional laser treatment of scars from acne, surgery, injury, or other causes. The laser creates micro-channels to stimulate collagen remodeling and improve scar texture, color, and flexibility. Healing involves both surface recovery and deep tissue regeneration over several months.

instructions.general_directive: Follow this phased guidance for optimal scar improvement. The first 2 weeks focus on wound healing, followed by 3-6 months of collagen remodeling.

sections.title: Pre-Treatment Preparation
sections.content: Stop retinoids, acids, and bleaching creams 1 week prior. For facial scars, antiviral prophylaxis if prone to cold sores. For darker skin types, pre-treatment hydroquinone may be recommended.

sections.title: Phase 1: Acute Healing (Days 0-14)
items: Immediate: Redness, swelling, pinpoint bleeding. Sandpaper texture.
Days 1-5: Keep treated area moist with healing ointment. Cleanse gently 2-3x daily with saline or mild cleanser.
Days 5-14: Skin darkens, then peels/flakes. DO NOT PICK. Allow natural exfoliation.
Signs of infection: Increasing pain, pus, spreading redness, fever.

sections.title: Phase 2: Remodeling & Results (Weeks 2-24+)
items: Weeks 2-8: Pink color fades. Scar may feel tighter initially, then soften.
Months 2-6: True collagen remodeling occurs. Scar texture gradually improves, elevation flattens, color normalizes.
SUN PROTECTION CRITICAL: UV exposure can permanently darken scars. SPF 30-50+ daily for 6+ months.

sections.title: Scar-Specific Care
items: Scar Massage: Begin gentle massage with vitamin E oil or silicone gel after 3-4 weeks (once fully healed). Massage 5-10 minutes, 2x daily to improve pliability.
Silicone Sheets/Gel: Start after 4 weeks. Wear sheets 12+ hours daily or apply gel 2x daily. Continue for 3-6 months.
Pressure Garments: If prescribed, begin wearing after 2-3 weeks as directed.

sections.title: Activity Restrictions
items: Avoid stretching or tension on the scar area for 4-6 weeks.
No swimming until fully healed (2+ weeks).
Avoid direct sun exposure for 3+ months.

sections.title: Scar Type & Expected Response
items: Discoloration: Redness improves fastest; brown discoloration may take longer.
Old vs. New scars: Newer scars (<1 year) respond better than older ones.

sections.title: Treatment Series & Follow-up
sections.content: Most scars require 3-5 treatments spaced 4-8 weeks apart. Follow-up at 3 months to assess collagen response and plan additional sessions. Maintenance treatments may be needed annually for optimal results.

patient_declaration.reading_confirmation: Scar improvement is a gradual process requiring consistent care over several months.
patient_declaration.question_opportunity: Ask about combining laser with other scar treatments (subcision, filler) for optimal results.
patient_declaration.declaration_text: I understand scar reduction requires multiple treatments and final results won't be visible for 3-6 months.
